note: Main GST rates are 5% and 18%, with 40% for luxury and sin goods. The 12% and 28% slabs were removed.
A goods transport agency (GTA) charges either 5% without input tax credit (ITC) or 18% with full ITC. The earlier 12% option no longer exists.
Interest on tax paid late is 18% a year, on the net tax paid in cash, from the day after the due date to the date of payment.
Interest on input tax credit wrongly availed and utilised is 18% a year. No interest arises if the credit was availed but not used.
Late fee is Rs 50 a day (Rs 25 CGST + Rs 25 SGST) where tax is payable, and Rs 20 a day for nil returns, capped at Rs 500 for nil returns.
Late fee caps per return: Rs 2,000 for turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore, Rs 5,000 for Rs 1.5-5 crore, Rs 10,000 above Rs 5 crore.
Monthly GSTR-1 is due on the 11th and GSTR-3B on the 20th of the next month. Quarterly (QRMP) GSTR-1 is due on the 13th after the quarter.

Registration is needed above Rs 20 lakh aggregate turnover, or Rs 40 lakh for suppliers of goods only in states that adopted the higher limit. Any inter-state supply of goods needs registration whatever the turnover.
Composition is open to traders and manufacturers with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore, at 1%; restaurants pay 5%. Composition dealers cannot collect tax or claim ITC.
ITC for a financial year must be claimed in a return filed by 30 November of the next year, or the annual return date if earlier.
ITC can be claimed only on invoices that appear in GSTR-2B, after receipt of goods or services.
ITC must be reversed for any amount not paid to the supplier within 180 days of the invoice date, and can be re-availed on payment.
ITC on motor vehicles carrying persons with up to 13 seats is blocked, except for further supply, passenger transport or driving training.
ITC on food, beverages and outdoor catering is blocked, unless used for the same category of outward supply or required to be provided by law.
Government buyers deduct 2% GST TDS on contracts above Rs 2,50,000, excluding tax. The deductor files GSTR-7 by the 10th of the next month.
E-commerce operators collect tax at source at 0.5% of net taxable supplies: 0.25% CGST plus 0.25% SGST for intra-state supplies, or 0.5% IGST for inter-state supplies, from 10 July 2024.
citation: Section 52, CGST Act; Notification 15/2024-Central Tax and 01/2024-Integrated Tax

note: Cars over 4,000 mm, or with petrol engines above 1,200 cc or diesel engines above 1,500 cc, are taxed at 40%. Small cars are at 18%. Compensation cess on cars ended.
Rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per night are at 5% without ITC. Above Rs 7,500 they are at 18% with ITC.
New regime slabs: 0-4 lakh nil, 4-8 lakh 5%, 8-12 lakh 10%, 12-16 lakh 15%, 16-20 lakh 20%, 20-24 lakh 25%, above 24 lakh 30%; cess 4%.
Salaried employees get a standard deduction of Rs 75,000 in the new regime and Rs 50,000 in the old regime.
In the new regime, tax is fully rebated if taxable income does not exceed Rs 12 lakh. Just above Rs 12 lakh, marginal relief caps tax at the income above Rs 12 lakh.
Old regime (below 60): 0-2.5 lakh nil, 2.5-5 lakh 5%, 5-10 lakh 20%, above 10 lakh 30%, plus 4% cess. Rebate up to Rs 12,500 if taxable income is up to Rs 5 lakh.
citation: Section 87A, Income-tax Act 1961 (FY 2025-26); Section 156, Income-tax Act 2025 (from 1 April 2026)

note: Salary TDS is under Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1 April 2026; Section 192 of the 1961 Act applies to FY 2025-26 and earlier.
From tax year 2026-27: Form 130 replaces Form 16; Form 138 replaces 24Q; Form 122 replaces 12B; Form 123 replaces 12BA; Form 124 replaces 12BB.
TDS deducted in a month is deposited by the 7th of the next month; TDS deducted in March by 30 April.
Quarterly salary TDS statements are due 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May for Q1 to Q4.
The EPF wage ceiling is Rs 25,000 a month for wage months from 17 September 2026, and Rs 15,000 for earlier wage months.
Employee and employer each contribute 12% of PF wages. Of the employer share, 8.33% goes to the pension scheme (EPS) on wages up to the pension ceiling, and the rest to EPF.
EPF and ESI contributions for a wage month are due by the 15th of the next month.
ESI covers employees with wages up to Rs 21,000 a month (Rs 25,000 for persons with disability). The employee pays 0.75% and the employer 3.25%.

Gratuity = last drawn wages x 15/26 x completed years of service, where a part year of more than six months counts as a full year. Five years' continuous service is needed, except on death or disablement, and one year for fixed-term employees.

Statutory gratuity and its tax exemption for non-government employees are capped at Rs 20,00,000. The exemption sat in Section 10(10) of the 1961 Act up to tax year 2025-26 and is in the Income-tax Act 2025 from 1 April 2026.
If excluded items such as HRA and conveyance exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is added back to wages for PF, gratuity and bonus.
Wages due on resignation, removal, dismissal or retrenchment must be paid within two working days of the employee leaving.
Overtime is paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages.

Bonus is payable to employees drawing wages up to Rs 21,000 a month who worked at least 30 days in the accounting year; minimum 8.33% and maximum 20%, computed as if wages were Rs 7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher.
Meal vouchers are tax-free up to Rs 50 per meal up to FY 2025-26 and up to Rs 200 per meal from tax year 2026-27.
An invoice number can have at most 16 characters, using letters, numbers, hyphen and slash, unique within the financial year.
Turnover up to Rs 5 crore: 4-digit HSN on B2B invoices. Above Rs 5 crore: 6-digit HSN on all invoices.
For an unregistered buyer with taxable value of Rs 50,000 or more, the invoice must show name, address, delivery address and state.
E-invoicing applies if aggregate turnover exceeded Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18. It covers B2B invoices, exports, credit notes and debit notes.
Taxpayers with turnover of Rs 10 crore or more must report invoices, credit notes and debit notes to the IRP within 30 days of their date.
Where e-invoicing applies, an invoice without an IRN is not a valid tax invoice, and the buyer cannot claim ITC on it.
An IRN can be cancelled on the IRP within 24 hours of generation; after that, issue a credit note.
Insurers, banks, financial institutions including NBFCs, GTAs, passenger transport operators, multiplex admissions, SEZ units and government departments are exempt from e-invoicing.
A service invoice must be issued within 30 days of supply; banks, insurers and NBFCs have 45 days.
An invoice for goods must be issued before or at the time of removal, or of delivery where the supplier does not move the goods.
A credit note reduces output tax only if declared by 30 November after the end of the financial year of supply, or the annual return date if earlier.
An e-way bill is needed when consignment value, including GST, exceeds Rs 50,000. Inter-state job-work movement needs one whatever the value.

E-way bill validity: normal cargo 1 day per 200 km or part; over-dimensional cargo 1 day per 20 km or part. A day is a 24-hour period counted from midnight of the day of generation, so a 1-day bill expires at midnight of the next day.
An e-way bill can be extended within 8 hours before or after expiry, and cancelled within 24 hours of generation.
Packing, freight and other incidental charges billed by the supplier are part of the taxable value.
Interest or late fee charged to a buyer for delayed payment is part of the value of supply and is taxed at the rate of the main supply.
Costs paid on the client's behalf as a pure agent, recovered at actual cost and shown separately, are excluded from value.
TDS on professional fees is 10% once payments in the year exceed Rs 50,000, on the fee excluding GST shown separately. Section 194J for FY 2025-26; Section 393 from 1 April 2026.
citation: Section 194J, Income-tax Act 1961; Section 393, Income-tax Act 2025

note: From tax year 2026-27: Form 140 replaces Form 26Q, Form 131 replaces Form 16A, and Form 144 replaces Form 27Q.
